g.text: ADR-003: Source-agnostic trials, documents and gold datasets
How do we store trials, documents and gold labels so that sources can change, nothing is stored twice, every change is traceable, and a check can
be evaluated against any gold dataset?
what forces this decision now: facts and constraints, no solutions
• Everything is CTIS-shaped today: ctis.* tables, CTIS document types, CTIS snapshots. A trial from ClinicalTrials.gov, a journal publication or a document added by
• Checks read only the CTIS summary of results, but a trial's results can be in any document linked to it.
• Bruckner et al.'s labels sit in the working database (gold.bruckner_*) and the workflow selects trials with --reviewed. They are our benchmark, to be used only in
tests, CI and after changes to retrieval, prompts, model settings or code, and the benchmark itself may grow or be replaced.
• The same PDF is already stored under several documents (e.g. a lay summary and a summary of results with the same bytes); the same trial may come from several
• Nobody can tell who added a trial, a document or a link, or when. Judgements by a person (ADR-001: undecided goes to a person) have no home.
• Comparing our check with reviewers who read different documents produces false 'false accusations', the costliest error (ADR-001).
2–3 real options; the current proposal is only one of them
How it works: keep ctis.*, add ctgov.*, pubmed.*,
manual.*, gold.<dataset>_*; checks and scoring join
• each source keeps its own shape
• every check, page and score grows a branch per
• each gold dataset needs its own scoring code
How it works: central trial, document and gold
tables; one adapter per source fills them; sources
keep their raw records beside them; Postgres writes
• checks, pages and scoring see one shape
• a new source or gold set is an adapter, not a
• identity matching must be designed carefully
How it works: one table of JSON documents keyed by
(source, key, kind); views and code interpret them.
• no constraints: duplicates and broken links are
• queries and checks parse JSON everywhere
• the audit and versioning rules live only in code
+ better · 0 no difference · – worse, and a few words why
+ every linked document, one identity per
Cost: money, tokens, time per run
– reviewers and check may read different
+ evidence scope fixed per gold dataset;
Effort: to build and to maintain
Undo: how hard to reverse later
+ audit log by triggers, actors, versions
what we chose and which criteria decided it
We choose B, central model + source adapters, because it is the only option that gives every check all documents linked to a trial (quality), lets reviewers and check
read the same evidence (risk, ADR-001), and records who did what (traceability). Its cost is a one-off rebuild, which we take now while the local data is reset
1. Sources: a source table (registry, publication index, manual, gold); every stored record carries (source, the source's own key), unique, so re-fetching versions it
2. Trials: trial = our id; trial_identifier (scheme, normalised value) is unique and points to one trial; trial_record = what one source says, versioned. Ingest
matches all identifiers: none → new trial, one trial → attach, several → a possible duplicate for a person; merges are recorded and reversible.
3. Documents in three layers: file (bytes, by sha256, stored once) → document (logical, identity = source key) → document version (replaced files kept, dated). Same
text in different bytes is flagged by a page-text fingerprint. Trial ↔ document links carry role, basis (listed by the registry, identifier in the text, by hand),
source and confidence; a check reads the current version of every linked document and records which.
4. Audit: actors (people and processes); an append-only audit log written by Postgres triggers in the same transaction; no update in place or hard delete without an
5. Gold datasets: dataset version (name, version, source, evidence scope) and items naming trials by identifier, with labels, comments and subsets (dev/test). An
evaluation = dataset version + subset + pipeline configuration; it runs in its own database built from a bundle (trials, files, labels), so CI is reproducible and the
working database never holds benchmark data. CI replays stored model answers on every push and makes real model calls when prompts or model settings change, or by
hand. Bruckner et al. is the first gold source.
Easier: adding a registry, publications or manual entry (an adapter); a new or
larger gold dataset (a converter + its evidence scope); fair evaluation; seeing
who added what; CI on fixed inputs; manual judgements next to automatic ones.
Harder: one schema rebuild now and a local database reset; identity matching
needs care and a person for conflicts; bundles (~300 MB of PDFs for Bruckner et
al.) live outside git; every write path must set an actor.
Revisit when: identity matching produces many conflicts a person can't keep up
with; a source can't be expressed as trial records + documents; evaluation
bundles grow too large to rebuild per CI run.
Lab: migrations for sources, actors, audit, trials and documents; the CTIS
adapter; `trialwatch eval` on the Bruckner bundle with zero new false
Decided with the user on 2026-11-18: back up the local database (pg_dump) and start from scratch; gold data only in evaluation databases; manual check = a person's
judgement and starting an automatic check by hand; every automatic check keeps a step-by-step trace for the web interface. Rejected: merging duplicate trials
automatically when identifiers conflict (a wrong merge mixes two trials' results).
How to use: copy to docs/adr/ADR-NNN-name.excalidraw · replace the grey text (set it to black) · status chip colour: orange open, yellow proposed, green accepted, grey
superseded · one page: if it doesn't fit, the decision is too big, so split it.
